description: Published adapter capability matrix (goal.md §13.1). Levels: A0 package/version detection, A1 build/typecheck/test observation, A2 static symbol resolution, A3 runtime symbol instrumentation, A4 clean Sample + Contract verification. No adapter pretends a level it does not have.

adapters.name: node-typescript
adapters.notes: Reference ecosystem. Lockfile-resolved versions (package-lock v2/v3, pnpm-lock v9, yarn classic). Static import/member analysis without a type checker yields PROBABLE symbols; EXACT reserved for future TS type-info integration. Verifier adapter node-typescript@1 supports clean resolve/compile/contract. Verification runs on the runtime the sample declares, not on Node by assumption: node:22-alpine, oven/bun:1-alpine or denoland/deno:alpine, each pinned to an immutable image digest rather than run from the floating tag, so the execution-context axis (docs/execution-context.md) carries real bun and deno results rather than node for everything.

adapters.name: python
adapters.notes: Resolved versions from uv.lock, pinned requirements, poetry.lock (best-effort). AST-free regex import analysis; dynamic attribute access degrades to UNKNOWN. Sample verification uses python:3.12-slim when runtimeVersion is omitted or 3.12, and the digest-pinned python:3.14-slim@sha256:cae66f2ef0ec51a9891263eeee7f987dacf0a9879e8aa9353d5606e0530619a5 when runtimeVersion is 3.14. Debian rather than Alpine: musl cannot use a manylinux wheel, so a package that publishes manylinux only falls back to an sdist build the Alpine image has no toolchain for. Packages that also publish musllinux wheels installed there fine. Other Python lines are rejected before claim. pip resolves into the workspace vendor directory so the offline contract stage can import it (A4, proven by published samples).

adapters.name: go
adapters.notes: go.mod/go.sum resolved versions; go/parser import + selector analysis. EXACT requires go/types integration, not claimed in v1. Sample verification now runs in the digest-pinned golang:1.26-alpine image with GOMODCACHE inside the workspace, so `go run` compiles offline in the contract stage (A4, proven by published samples).

adapters.name: rust
adapters.notes: Cargo.lock resolved versions; use-statement analysis. Macro-expanded and dynamic usage degrades to UNKNOWN (goal.md §13.5 conservative start). Sample verification now runs in the digest-pinned rust:1-alpine image with CARGO_HOME inside the workspace, so `cargo run --offline` builds in the contract stage (A4, proven by published samples).

adapters.name: php
adapters.notes: Verification-only adapter. Both stages run in the digest-pinned composer:2 image on purpose: composer writes vendor/composer/platform_check.php from the PHP version it resolved under, so resolving in one image and testing in another couples two tags that drift independently. Resolve uses --no-scripts --no-plugins, the composer equivalent of npm's --ignore-scripts: composer.json is data, but the scripts and plugins inside it are code and would otherwise run with the network on. No local project scanner yet, so composer projects get no A0/A1/A2 detection and this adapter claims none. Verifier image: composer:2, pinned by digest.

adapters.name: ruby
adapters.notes: Verification-only adapter. Resolve installs bundler and runs bundle install with GEM_HOME, GEM_PATH, BUNDLE_PATH and BUNDLE_APP_CONFIG all inside the workspace, which is the only reason the gems survive into the network-off contract stage. No local project scanner yet, so Ruby projects get no A0/A1/A2 detection and this adapter claims none. Verifier image: ruby:3, pinned by digest. Debian and not Alpine on purpose: a gem with a C extension compiles at install time, every time, and Alpine ships no compiler, so the receipt records glibc for Ruby.

adapters.name: dart
adapters.notes: Verification-only adapter. Resolve runs dart pub get with PUB_CACHE inside the workspace so dart test runs offline. No local project scanner yet, so Dart and Flutter projects get no A0/A1/A2 detection and this adapter claims none. Verifier image: dart:3.13.0, pinned by digest.

adapters.name: elixir
adapters.notes: Verification-only adapter, and the one with a real constraint. mix.exs is executable Elixir and every mix task evaluates it, so `mix deps.get` would run the sample's own code while the network is up. Resolve therefore never lets mix see the project: it works from a scratch directory, reads the pinned package set out of mix.lock as TEXT, and fetches each one with mix hex.package fetch, which verifies the package checksum. A sample without a committed mix.lock cannot be verified. Because that skips mix's own .hex marker file, samples build and test with --no-deps-check. No local project scanner yet, so Elixir projects get no A0/A1/A2 detection and this adapter claims none. Verifier image: elixir:1.20.1-alpine, pinned by digest.

adapters.name: maven-java
adapters.notes: Verification-only Java adapter. The sample's pom.xml, .mvn directory, settings and build plugins are never used while networking is enabled. Exact canonical Maven purls in the manifest are the complete runtime lock (direct and companion JARs): CodeSampleX generates a fresh resolver POM and Central-only settings, runs only maven-dependency-plugin 3.9.0 from /tmp with transitive expansion disabled and strict checksums, then runs build/contract offline. An omitted runtime version preserves the legacy Maven 3.9 / Java 21 Temurin Alpine (musl) lane. Exact runtime versions 8, 11, 17, 21 and 25 select digest-pinned Maven 3.9.11 / Amazon Corretto / Amazon Linux 2023 (glibc) images. Other Java lines are rejected before claim rather than substituted. This deliberately excludes Maven classifiers/non-JAR packaging, SNAPSHOTs and dependency graphs not fully pinned in the manifest. Gradle contracts use the separate gradle-java@1 adapter. No local project scanner yet, so Maven projects get no A0/A1/A2 detection.

adapters.name: gradle-java
adapters.notes: Verification-only Gradle/Java adapter. The sample's build.gradle(.kts), settings.gradle(.kts), init scripts, wrapper, gradle.properties and plugins are never executed while networking is enabled. Exact canonical Maven purls are the complete JAR closure; ranges, dynamic + selectors, SNAPSHOTs, classifiers, non-JAR packaging and transitive expansion are rejected. CodeSampleX generates a Central-only Gradle resolver, runs it from /tmp with a clean workspace GRADLE_USER_HOME, verifies the resolved coordinate set, copies and hashes each JAR, then uses a second generated Gradle Java project for network-off compile and Contract execution. Exact Java 8, 11, 17 and 21 use digest-pinned Gradle 8.14.3 / Amazon Corretto / Amazon Linux 2023 (glibc) images; Java 25 uses Gradle 9.7.0 in the same image family and therefore is not classified as a pure-JDK comparison with the earlier lines. Omitted and unsupported runtime versions are rejected before claim. No local Java/Gradle project scanner exists, so this adapter claims no A0/A1/A2.

adapters.name: unreal
adapters.notes: Recognises an Unreal Engine project by its .uproject and reports the engine it targets as the public coordinate engine/unreal. It claims no packages, deliberately: Unreal's dependencies are engine modules and marketplace plugins and neither has a stable public identifier this network could hold anyone to, so any package coordinate here would be invented. The engine version is read from EngineAssociation and is required -- a source build writes a GUID there, and a descriptor that cannot become a coordinate produces no hint at all. There is no verification lane and there is not going to be one from this adapter: the verifier runs contracts in a fixed 512MB linux container with no network, and an Unreal build needs tens of gigabytes, Windows and a licence.

runtimeInstrumentation: A3 is not provided by any Public v1 adapter (goal.md §19).
